There were no supplied candidates, so this was a discovery pass over lines 1–123. I did not open the imported files.

The only visible overlap is between `exists_signedEquiv_and_lattice_map_monomialEquiv_iff` and `exists_signedEquiv_and_integralLatticeIsometry_iff`. Both prove the forward direction with `rintro ⟨v, hv, _⟩; exact (exists_signed_monomialEquiv_iff u e).mp ⟨v, hv⟩`. Both start the backward direction with `obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := (exists_signed_monomialEquiv_iff u e).mpr hu`, then `rw`, then a final `exact`.

I judged this a thin wrapper around `exists_signed_monomialEquiv_iff`, not nontrivial repeated reasoning. The two theorems have different existential payloads: a lattice-map equality in one, and a dual-containment proof, an isometry and its apply-equality in the other. A shared lemma would need to abstract over an arbitrary predicate on `v` and would save only a few lines. This is also the "moving duplicated branches inside a helper" case the rubric excludes. Both final steps are single applications of existing lemmas: `lattice_map_signedEquiv`, and `map_signedEquiv_le_euclideanDual` with `integralLatticeSignedEquiv` and `integralLatticeSignedEquiv_apply`.

The `Or` case-split with `Units.ext` in `monomialEquiv_preserves_form_iff_exists_signed` is a short routine calculation and appears only once in this file. `form_monomialEquiv_iff` is a single-use argument that relies on the imported `dotProduct_monomialEquiv_iff`.
